plain.headline: Christ Our King
plain.intro: On this last Sunday of the Church year, we celebrate Jesus Christ as King of the Universe. The readings show what kind of king he is: a shepherd who searches for the lost and heals the hurt, the risen Lord who defeats even death, and a judge who tells us that whatever we did for the least of his brothers and sisters, we did for him. Next Sunday, Advent begins a new Church year.
plain.listen: where the King says he was all along

Reading 1.box: Ezekiel spoke to God's people in exile in Babylon, after their own leaders had cared for themselves instead of the flock. God promises to be their shepherd himself: to search for the lost, heal the injured, and judge with justice. Ezekiel prophesied about 600 years before Christ.

chunks.text: The Lord God says this: 'I myself will search for my sheep and look after them. As a shepherd looks for his scattered flock, so I will look for my sheep. I will rescue them from every place where they were scattered on that dark and cloudy day.

I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will give them rest, says the Lord God. I will look for the lost and bring back the strays. I will bandage the injured and make the sick strong. But the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will feed them with justice.'
As for you, my flock, the Lord God says this: 'I will judge between one sheep and another, between rams and goats.'

Responsorial Psalm.box: In this beloved psalm, the Lord is the shepherd who leads, feeds, and protects us. His goodness and love follow us every day, and we will live in his house forever.

Reading 2.box: Paul teaches that the risen Christ is the first of a great harvest, and all who belong to him will rise too. Christ reigns until every enemy is defeated, death last of all, and then hands the Kingdom to the Father so that God may be all in all. This does not make the Son less than the Father; it speaks of Christ, who became man, offering his finished work to the Father.

chunks.text: But Christ has in fact been raised from the dead, the first fruits of all who have died. Since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead also came through a man. Just as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be brought to life.

But each in the right order: Christ first, then, when he comes, those who belong to him. Then comes the end, when he hands over the Kingdom to God the Father, after he has destroyed every ruler, every authority, and every power.

For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. The last enemy to be destroyed is death. When everything has been placed under him, then the Son himself will also be placed under the Father, who put everything under him, so that God may be all in all.

Gospel.box: These are the last words of Jesus' teaching in Matthew's Gospel before his Passion. The King on the throne is Jesus himself, and he judges the nations by how they treated people in need, because he is present in them. Much of the Church's list of works of mercy, such as feeding the hungry and visiting the sick, comes from this passage.

chunks.text: "When the Son of Man comes in his glory, with all the angels, he will sit on his glorious throne. All the nations will be gathered in front of him, and he will separate them from each other, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. He will put the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.

Then the King will say to those on his right, 'Come, you whom my Father has blessed. Receive the Kingdom prepared for you since the world was made. For I was hungry and you gave me food. I was thirsty and you gave me a drink. I was a stranger and you welcomed me. I needed clothes and you clothed me. I was sick and you cared for me. I was in prison and you visited me.'

Then the righteous will answer, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink? When did we see you a stranger and welcome you, or without clothes and clothe you? When did we see you sick or in prison and visit you?' The King will answer, 'I tell you the truth, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.'

Then he will say to those on his left, 'Go away from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry and you gave me no food. I was thirsty and you gave me nothing to drink. I was a stranger and you did not welcome me. I needed clothes and you did not clothe me. I was sick and in prison and you did not visit me.'

They will answer, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty, a stranger or without clothes, sick or in prison, and not help you?' He will answer, 'I tell you the truth, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for me.' And they will go away to eternal punishment, but the righteous to eternal life."

plain.carry: This week I will look for Christ the King in someone who is hungry, lonely, sick, or left out, and do one concrete thing to serve him there.

kids.headline: Jesus Is Our King
kids.intro: Today is the feast of Christ the King, the last Sunday of the Church's year. Jesus is a different kind of king. He is like a good shepherd who looks for lost sheep, and he tells us that when we help someone in need, we are helping him.
kids.listen: what the King says people did for him

Reading 1.box: God's people had leaders who did not take care of them, like bad shepherds who ignore their sheep. So God promises that he himself will be their shepherd. He will find the lost ones and take care of the hurt ones.

chunks.text: God says, "I will go looking for my sheep myself. Like a shepherd who looks for sheep that wandered away, I will look for mine. I will rescue them from every place they ran off to on that dark, cloudy day.

I will be their shepherd and let them rest. I will find the lost sheep and bring back the ones that wandered off. I will bandage the hurt ones and make the sick ones strong. But I will put an end to the fat, strong ones who pushed the others around. I will be fair to my whole flock, and I will judge between one sheep and another."

Responsorial Psalm.box: This is one of the most famous songs in the Bible. It says God is our shepherd who gives us everything we need, leads us to green grass and calm water, and keeps us close forever.

Reading 2.box: Saint Paul says Jesus was the first to rise from the dead, and everyone who belongs to him will rise too. Jesus is King over everything, and in the end he will even defeat death.

chunks.text: Jesus really did rise from the dead. He is the first, like the first fruit picked at harvest time. Death came into the world through one man, Adam. New life came through one man, Jesus. Because of Jesus, everyone who belongs to him will be made alive when he comes again.

At the very end, Jesus will defeat every power that is against God. He will be King until all his enemies are beaten. The last enemy he will defeat is death. Then Jesus will give his whole Kingdom to God the Father, so that God will be everything to everyone.

Gospel.box: Jesus tells what will happen when he comes again as King at the end of time. He will gather everyone and look at how they treated people who were hungry, sick, lonely, or in need. Jesus says that whatever we do for them, we do for him.

chunks.text: Jesus said, "When the Son of Man comes in glory with all the angels, he will sit on his throne as King. All the people of the world will gather in front of him. He will separate them, the way a shepherd separates sheep from goats, with the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.

Then the King will say to the people on his right, 'Come, my Father has blessed you. Come into the Kingdom he made ready for you. When I was hungry, you fed me. When I was thirsty, you gave me a drink. When I was a stranger, you welcomed me. When I needed clothes, you gave them to me. When I was sick, you took care of me. When I was in prison, you came to see me.'

The good people will ask, 'Lord, when did we ever see you hungry or thirsty, or a stranger, or needing clothes, or sick, or in prison, and help you?' The King will answer, 'Whenever you did it for one of the least of my brothers and sisters, you did it for me.'

Then the King will say to the people on his left, 'Go away from me, into the fire that never ends, which was made for the devil and his angels. When I was hungry, you did not feed me. When I was thirsty, you gave me nothing to drink. When I was a stranger, you did not welcome me. When I needed clothes, or was sick, or in prison, you did not come to help me.'

They will ask, 'Lord, when did we see you in need and not help you?' He will answer, 'Whenever you did not help one of the least of these, you did not help me.' Those people will go away to be punished forever, but the good people will go into life with God that never ends."

word.meaning: A king is a ruler who leads and protects his people. Jesus is King of everything, and he rules with love.

kids.draw: Draw Jesus the King on his throne, and around him draw people helping someone who is hungry, sick, or lonely.
kids.ask: Who is someone you could help this week, knowing that you are helping Jesus too?

family.opener: Today is the feast of Christ the King, and Jesus tells us that we meet him, our King, in every person who needs our help.
questions: What kind of king is Jesus, and how is he different from other kings or rulers we hear about?
Why do you think the people in the story were surprised to learn they had helped Jesus?
Who in our neighborhood, school, or parish might be hungry, lonely, or sick, and how could we help?
family.try: Choose one work of mercy to do together this week, such as bringing food to a food pantry, calling or visiting someone who is sick or alone, or giving away clothes you no longer need.
family.pray: Jesus, our King and Good Shepherd, help our family see you in everyone we meet and serve you with loving hearts.
